paper_metadata.title: Benchmarking the performance of portfolio optimization with QAOA

summary: The paper benchmarks QAOA for portfolio optimization using real DAX‑30 market data with 5‑ and 10‑asset instances (5–10 qubits). In noiseless simulations, the full XY and QAMPA mixers reach approximation ratios >0.99 for n=5 and about 0.98 with ~0.6 probability of the optimal portfolio for n=10 at depth p=7. The study also analyzes noise effects using depolarizing channels and shows that simpler mixers can outperform XY mixers under higher noise.

experiments.description: QAOA portfolio optimization benchmark comparing standard mixer, four XY-mixer variants (ring, parity ring, full, QAMPA), and different classical optimizers on real DAX market instances under ideal and noisy simulation.

algorithm.variant: QAOA for portfolio optimization with standard mixer and XY-mixer variants (ring, parity ring, full, QAMPA)
algorithm.ansatz: QAOA alternating phase-separation and mixer layers; XY-mixer uses Dicke-state initial state; QAMPA reorders mixer and phase gates
algorithm.optimizer: SLSQP for statevector simulations; Nelder-Mead for qasm simulations; COBYLA for noisy density-matrix simulations in Sec. 4.3
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Classical optimizer run until its internal stopping criterion / max iterations; for Nelder-Mead max iterations limited to 10 times number of parameters

hyperparameters.budget_B: 2 for n=5 instances; 5 for n=10 instances
hyperparameters.penalty_factor_A: chosen by classical procedure; example A=0.2 in easy/hard analysis; otherwise instance-dependent
hyperparameters.global_scaling_factor_lambda: chosen so that spectral width of F matches mixer M; example lambda=6 in easy/hard analysis
hyperparameters.max_depth_p: 7 in main mixer comparison; 6 in easy/hard analysis
hyperparameters.instance_count: 20 random instances for each of n=5 and n=10 benchmarks
hyperparameters.optimizer_restarts: 4 optimization runs per depth p (previous-depth extrapolation, linear ansatz, quadratic ansatz, zero-angles)

algorithm.parameter_initialization: For p=1, grid search over 100 logarithmically spaced (m1,m2) pairs; for p>1, extrapolation from previous depth plus three alternatives: linear ansatz, quadratic ansatz, and zero-angle initialization
algorithm.classical_baselines: Classical brute-force search for feasible portfolios to compute F_min and F_max and determine optimal solutions for small n

problem_formulation.encoding_details: One qubit per binary asset-selection variable z_i ∈ {0,1}; feasible portfolios satisfy sum_i z_i = B
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize F(z)=1/2 * sum_{i,j} z_i z_j sigma_ij - (1-q) * sum_i z_i mu_i, subject to sum_i z_i = B; penalty version adds A*(sum_i z_i - B)^2
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Standard QAOA uses penalty term; XY-mixers enforce feasibility by preserving Hamming weight; QAMPA is a reordered full XY mixer
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: F(A)=F + A(sum_i z_i - B)^2 mapped to Ising form with Z operators; F = sum_{i<j} w_ij Z_i Z_j + sum_i w_i Z_i + constant

problem_instance.description: Portfolio selection on German stock market data; benchmark instances sampled from DAX 30 constituents

ticker_symbols: DAX constituents; appendix lists LINDE.DE, BAYN.DE, VNA.DE, MTX.DE, MUV2.DE for one 5-asset instance
dataset_specification.preprocessing: Daily percentage returns computed from historical prices; annualized returns and covariance matrix computed with factor 252

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Compute daily returns r_i(k)=(P_i(k)-P_i(k-1))/P_i(k-1); annualize returns and covariance with 252 trading days; normalize correlations to Pearson coefficients for hardness analysis
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 20 random instances for each benchmark size; compare approximation ratio and ground-state probability versus QAOA depth; noisy studies use density-matrix simulator with 8192 samples or qasm with 1000 shots; easy/hard analysis keeps 20 best and 20 worst of 2400 random baskets

noise_model.noise_type: measurement sampling noise in qasm simulator; depolarizing channel noise in density-matrix simulations

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical brute-force evaluation of feasible portfolios for Fmin/Fmax and penalty selection; scaling factor lambda chosen to match spectral widths
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute approximation ratio r and ground-state probability P from measured bitstrings

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: Approximation ratio and ground-state probability generally improve with depth; full XY and QAMPA converge fastest in ideal simulation

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper benchmarks QAOA performance but does not claim or demonstrate asymptotic quantum speedup.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Not explicitly characterized asymptotically for this portfolio-QAOA benchmark
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Not explicitly characterized asymptotically; brute-force used only for small n

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not estimated; authors speculate that several hundred qubits might be required for speedup based on prior Max‑Cut studies.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Likely hundreds of logical qubits and deeper QAOA circuits (p >> 7) with low noise; current experiments use only 5–10 qubits in simulation.
limiting_factors: Experiments limited to very small problem sizes (5–10 qubits/assets)
No comparison against scalable classical portfolio optimizers
Variational parameter optimization cost grows exponentially
Noise sensitivity of XY mixers on realistic hardware
No demonstrated runtime or complexity advantage

notes: hardware.type inferred as simulator_statevector because the paper explicitly uses Qiskit statevector simulator for ideal runs; qasm simulator and density-matrix simulator are also used in separate evaluations, but the paper does not name a real QPU.
num_qubits inferred from problem size n because the paper states n=5 and n=10 assets correspond to five and ten qubits.
circuit_depth inferred from reported QAOA depth p values.
speedup_order set to none_proven because the paper discusses performance benchmarking only and does not claim asymptotic quantum advantage.
The paper benchmarks QAOA variants but does not claim a demonstrated quantum advantage.
All results are obtained via classical simulation of quantum circuits with up to 10 qubits.
